versions.label: ESD coupon regulation (late 2020 through EIP-22)
versions.tokenRoles: ESD was transferable cash, bonded DAO stake and governance weight; epoch-indexed coupons represented burned principal plus a variable premium.
versions.backing: No external redemption reserve; USDC existed only in the Uniswap oracle/liquidity pair.
versions.redemption: Coupons became callable after two epochs, drew from expansion-created redeemable allocation, and expired after 90 epochs; later premiums were prorated.
versions.supplyPolicy: TWAP below $1 created debt capacity; users voluntarily burned ESD for coupons. TWAP above $1 reset debt and minted bounded expansion.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Aggregate debt ratio cap 20%; supply change generally 3%, 6% while coupon shortfall existed; epoch advance and bonded positions received minted rewards.
versions.oracle: USDC/ESD Uniswap V2 TWAP captured on manual epoch advance, with minimum oracle reserve and bootstrap override.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Bonded holders governed upgradeable DAO logic; lockups applied. Owner/commit upgrade route existed.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Uniswap V2 USDC/ESD price and LP pool; voluntary coupon buyers; bonded ESD and LP exit liquidity.

versions.label: Paused regulation and v1 migration path
versions.tokenRoles: Legacy ESD remained transferable; later implementation supported v2 migrator burning and pool withdrawals.
versions.redemption: Legacy coupon behavior was progressively removed/migrated; exact holder outcomes not reconstructed.
versions.supplyPolicy: Regulation was paused, bonding later removed, and migration enabled.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Migration initializer minted an advance incentive and development stake while moving pool assets to v2 control.
versions.oracle: Legacy oracle addresses remained recorded; active use after pause is not established.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Proposal commits upgraded implementation and assigned v2 DAO ownership.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Legacy pool withdrawal and v2 migration contracts.

incidents.summary: ESD entered a prolonged under-peg period around late December; secondary retrospective data later placed it near $0.23.
incidents.beneficiaries: Earlier sellers and recipients of prior expansion rewards
incidents.lossBearers: Residual ESD holders and coupon buyers
incidents.outcome: Peg did not sustainably recover; regulation was paused in April 2021.

versions.label: DSD 2020 coupon system
versions.tokenRoles: DSD was cash and bonded governance stake; coupons were epoch-indexed claims created by voluntarily burning DSD.
versions.backing: No collateral or external redemption asset.
versions.redemption: Coupons expired after 360 two-hour epochs (30 days); expansion first served coupons, then bonded/LP rewards.
versions.supplyPolicy: Project materials describe up to 10% per-epoch expansion/contraction using TWAP price gap and debt issuance below peg.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Coupon discount varied with debt ratio; post-debt expansion reportedly split 60% bonded DAO and 40% LP/oracle; advance caller received minted DSD.
versions.oracle: One-epoch, two-hour Uniswap TWAP, manually advanced.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Bonded token governance; 1% bonded DAO proposal threshold was documented. Exact upgrade authorities unresolved.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Uniswap DSD/USDC pool, bonded demand and voluntary coupon buyers.

incidents.summary: Contemporary report recorded a fall as low as $0.27 and partial recovery; later commentary acknowledged continuing under-peg conditions.
incidents.outcome: No durable peg recovery or definitive shutdown date established.

versions.label: Basis Cash v1/BIP-3/BIP-4 Treasury
versions.tokenRoles: BAC cash; BAB non-expiring discounted bond; BAS boardroom/share and incentive token.
versions.backing: No external reserve backing BAC or BAB; deposited bootstrap stablecoins were farming inputs, not redemption collateral.
versions.redemption: BAB burned for 1 BAC only above the curve ceiling and only to the extent of Treasury BAC balance.
versions.supplyPolicy: Below $1 burn BAC for amount/price BAB within bond cap. Above ceiling mint price-gap seigniorage.
versions.debtAndIncentives: Seigniorage: 2% community fund, reserve against BAB (80% if an epoch entirely debt-funded), remainder via proxy/boardroom. Bootstrap distributed 50,000 BAC over five days.
versions.oracle: Separate fixed-window Uniswap V2 bond and seigniorage oracles, explicitly updated around Treasury actions.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Treasury/token operator and ownership controls; timelock and migration functions; fund rate configurable by authorized control.
versions.liquidityDependencies: BAC/DAI pools, oracle reserves, boardroom BAS stake, BAB buyers, and continued demand for BAC.

versions.label: Basis Cash v2 migration and demand programs
versions.tokenRoles: BAC/BAB continued; BAS migrated to v2 and new vault/farm/bondroom incentives were added.
versions.backing: Roadmap proposed arbitrage vault and lending demand; no evidence of unconditional external redemption backing.
versions.redemption: Legacy Treasury/BAB gate remained economically dependent on expansion; exact v2 contract routing not fully reconstructed.
versions.supplyPolicy: Added liquidity and incentive layers rather than replacing the endogenous seigniorage core.
versions.debtAndIncentives: New BAS reward allocation, Curve/stableswap liquidity, vault/farms and bondroom.
versions.oracle: Multiple pools/oracles contemplated; complete v2 oracle map unresolved.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: Migration and reward allocation controlled through v2 governance/admin contracts.

incidents.summary: BIP-X proposed new liquidity and borrowing demand after stability problems; contemporary strategist described BAC under peg.
incidents.lossBearers: BAC holders, BAB holders if gate stayed closed, BAS holders whose seigniorage was subordinated
incidents.outcome: V2 launched, but no definitive shutdown/final mint date was established and peg failure persisted.

versions.label: BUILD Finance Basis Gold launch
versions.tokenRoles: BSG synthetic gold cash; BSGB discounted bond; BSGS boardroom shares; BUILD governance.
versions.backing: No vaulted gold or fiat; target was oracle-referenced, not collateral-backed.
versions.redemption: BSGB redeemed 1:1 BSG above target subject to Treasury balance; no gold redemption right.
versions.supplyPolicy: Burn BSG below target for discounted BSGB; mint BSG above target, reserve for bonds, then pay shares.
versions.debtAndIncentives: 2% initial expansion allocation to BUILD-controlled fund and 98% after bond funding to BSGS; 50 BSG bootstrap and one million BSGS farming schedule.
versions.oracle: Combination of Uniswap BSG market TWAP and Chainlink XAU/USD reference.
versions.governanceAndAdmin: BUILD governance controlled fund and could change the seigniorage percentage; Treasury/operator ownership paths in code.
versions.liquidityDependencies: Shallow BSG/DAI and BSGS/DAI pools, Chainlink XAU/USD, voluntary BSGB buyers.

claims.statement: ESD published Ethereum token, DAO, oracle, USDC pair and LP pool addresses; the token explorer reports verified source.
claims.evidenceLocator: README mainnet contracts; explorer Contract tab
claims.reasoning: Publisher addresses agree with explorer token identity.
claims.uncertainty: DAO bytecode/version activation was not independently matched.

claims.statement: ESD used eight-hour epochs, a 90-epoch bootstrap at $1.10, manual advance incentives, exit lockups and oracle reserve minimums in the selected January 2021 code.
claims.evidenceLocator: Constants.sol BOOTSTRAPPING_*, CURRENT_EPOCH_*, ADVANCE_INCENTIVE; Regulator.oracleCapture
claims.reasoning: Direct constants and control flow.
claims.uncertainty: Earlier launch parameters differed.

claims.statement: Coupon purchase burned user ESD, recorded principal and premium, required two epochs before redemption, and coupons expired after 90 epochs.
claims.evidenceLocator: Market.purchaseCoupons, redeemCoupons, step; Constants.COUPON_EXPIRATION
claims.reasoning: Direct code paths.

claims.statement: Below-peg oracle capture increased debt capacity; above peg reset debt and allocated bounded new supply, with later coupon premium proration.
claims.evidenceLocator: Regulator.shrinkSupply/growSupply/limit; Market.computeRedeemable
claims.reasoning: Direct code control flow.
claims.uncertainty: Comptroller allocation details summarized rather than exhaustively enumerated.

claims.statement: ESD and DSD entered durable under-peg states after late December 2020; retrospective synthesis reports approximately $0.23 and $0.24 respectively.
claims.evidenceLocator: case-study narrative and cited charts
claims.reasoning: Useful outcome evidence but price series was not independently reproduced.
claims.uncertainty: Exact timestamp, venue weighting and peak supplies require archival market/on-chain reconstruction.

claims.statement: ESD repository history records pause-regulation code on 2021-04-04, removal of bonding in July, and migration enablement on 2021-08-08.
claims.evidenceLocator: commits b4f24cb, 98dce0f, 1e9a7b2 and final Implementation.initialize
claims.reasoning: Commit history and code changes.
claims.uncertainty: Commit date is not guaranteed on-chain execution date.

claims.statement: In a permanent zero-demand state ESD coupons have no enforceable claim on USDC; their only payout source is conditional endogenous issuance, so coupon holders bear expiry/non-redemption risk.
claims.evidenceLocator: Market.redeemCoupons and Regulator.growSupply; absence of reserve transfer path
claims.reasoning: Cash-flow tracing shows mint-to-account redemption and no collateral seizure route.
claims.uncertainty: Does not model off-chain interventions.

claims.statement: Across coupon and Basis-family bond systems, burning current cash can reduce circulating ERC-20 supply while replacing it with a contingent economic claim; it does not itself create external assets or market demand.
claims.evidenceLocator: ESD purchaseCoupons; Basis Cash buyBonds; strategist's Full Impact/Fractional Impact argument
claims.reasoning: Comparative cash-flow analysis.
claims.uncertainty: Magnitude of price effect is market-dependent.

claims.statement: DSD token at 0xBD2F…66e3 is marked Source Code Verified Exact Match by Etherscan.
claims.evidenceLocator: Explorer Contract tab
claims.reasoning: Explorer verification statement.
claims.uncertainty: Does not verify the DAO.

claims.statement: DSD documented two-hour epochs, 360-epoch coupon expiry, manual advancement, one-epoch TWAP, and 60/40 bonded-versus-LP expansion rewards after coupon clearance.
claims.evidenceLocator: FAQ Token Mechanics and Maintaining the Peg sections
claims.reasoning: Contemporary project documentation.
claims.uncertainty: Canonical code commit was not recovered.

claims.statement: DSD claimed differentiation from ESD through 12 epochs/day and an uncapped price-difference formula apportioned across epochs, while elsewhere stating a maximum 10% per epoch.
claims.evidenceLocator: Protocol Core Dynamics and Differentiations from ESD
claims.reasoning: The page's 'not artificially capped' and 'max 10%' descriptions are internally ambiguous.
claims.uncertainty: Needs canonical historical code to resolve exact formula.

claims.statement: A contemporary mirror reported DSD fell to $0.27 on 2020-12-28 before trading near $0.63.
claims.evidenceLocator: post title and auto-generated summary
claims.reasoning: Contemporary timing but partial secondary retrieval.
claims.uncertainty: Original article and exchange-weighted data not retrieved.

claims.statement: A January 2021 Mith Cash strategist acknowledged ESD/DSD and MIC/BAC under-peg and argued bond conversion is weaker than spot buying because it often causes no new purchase.
claims.evidenceLocator: Background and Full Impact/Fractional Impact sections
claims.reasoning: Attributable contemporary argument, not adopted as quantitative proof.
claims.uncertainty: Author's affiliation and analysis are not independent protocol telemetry.

claims.statement: Basis Cash deployment manifest identifies BAC, BAB, BAS, Treasury, boardroom, bond oracle and seigniorage oracle addresses.

claims.statement: Basis Cash burned BAC and minted amount/price BAB below $1; BAB redemption was 1:1 BAC only above the ceiling and subject to Treasury BAC balance.
claims.evidenceLocator: Treasury.buyBonds and redeemBonds
claims.reasoning: Direct code paths and require gates.

claims.statement: Basis Cash expansion minted price-gap seigniorage, sent 2% to a fund, reserved against outstanding bonds, and distributed the remainder; fixed-window Uniswap oracles required periodic update.
claims.evidenceLocator: Treasury.allocateSeigniorage; Oracle.update/consult
claims.reasoning: Direct code.
claims.uncertainty: Boardroom proxy downstream distribution summarized.

claims.statement: Basis Cash announced 50,000 BAC over five bootstrap days to depositors of five existing stablecoins; these deposits were incentives, not BAC redemption reserves.
claims.evidenceLocator: README fair distribution and protocol description
claims.reasoning: README mechanism plus absence of collateral redemption path in Treasury.
claims.uncertainty: Distribution completion amounts not independently totaled.

claims.statement: BIP-X proposed Curve/stableswap migration, new BAS reward allocation, arbitrage vaults and BAC borrowing demand; official publication index dates v2 activation to 2021-04-26.
claims.evidenceLocator: BIP-X Phase 1; publication index Basis V2 launch
claims.reasoning: Proposal plus official activation announcement index.

claims.statement: Basis Cash v2 demand programs did not establish unconditional external-asset redemption for legacy BAB in the sources reviewed.

claims.reasoning: No collateral redemption path appears in legacy code or roadmap text.

claims.statement: BAB seniority was an issuance waterfall: future expansion funded bond reserves before boardroom surplus, but a persistent below-gate state supplied no redemption budget.
claims.evidenceLocator: allocateSeigniorage reserve order and redeemBonds gates
claims.reasoning: Control-flow and balance-source analysis.
claims.uncertainty: Treasury could theoretically receive discretionary transfers outside core policy.

claims.statement: Basis Gold announced BSG/BSGB/BSGS/BUILD roles, Ethereum addresses, January 14 distribution and January 21 stabilization, and identified Basis Cash as its base.
claims.evidenceLocator: How Basis Gold works, token distribution and launch information
claims.reasoning: Contemporary official launch announcement.
claims.uncertainty: Scheduled stabilization start not independently matched to transaction.

claims.statement: Basis Gold code burns BSG for discounted bonds below an XAU-derived target, gates 1:1 BSG redemption above target, and allocates expansion through fund, bond reserve and boardroom; it does not redeem gold.
claims.evidenceLocator: contracts/Treasury.sol buyBonds, redeemBonds, allocateSeigniorage; launch oracle description
claims.reasoning: Direct code plus target-oracle documentation; no gold transfer path exists.
claims.uncertainty: Deployment-bytecode equivalence not independently proven.

claims.reasoning: Primary proposal plus successor historical statement.
